units: field units; origin at the person, +x right, +y DOWN (screen), angles in degrees measured clockwise from +x, -90 = top
rounding: every emitted number is rounded to 6 decimals (Math.round(v * 1e6) / 1e6, -0 emitted as 0); a conforming implementation matches the golden vectors within 1e-6

drawn.rule: rho_drawn = drawn.min + (rho - body.min) / (body.max - body.min) * (drawn.max - drawn.min), with rho the V1 body radius (requirement mass). Monotone in weightSum; 34.2 … 54.6 field units: ≥ 56 … ≤ 92 px diameter at L0, 1920 × 1080, with the frame widened to hold every drawn body whole (PG-14).

rules: Bodies are placed one by one in rank order; a body at its fit position is taken as long as it keeps the collision distance to every body already placed.
Collision distance: centre distance >= rho_drawn(a) + rho_drawn(b) + body.gap (V1.1: the DRAWN radius — bodies must not touch as drawn). Overflow bodies are not drawn and take no part in collisions.
Radial candidates (in this order): offset 0, +1, -1, +2, -2 ... +-radialSteps, each offset k meaning distance = base + k * step, with step = 2 * rho_drawn + body.gap (V1.1).

Radial band, inclusive on both edges (V1.1: with rho = the MASS radius, unchanged from V1 — the band is a statement about fit, not about drawn size): a checked role may lie in [rings.bestFit, rings.horizon - rho]; a shelf role in [rings.shelfNear, field.radius - rho]. A candidate outside its band is skipped. A drawn body may therefore reach beyond its band edge (a shelf body across the field ring); it never touches another body.

At each radial candidate, angular candidates in this order: offset 0, +1, -1, +2, -2 ... +-angularSteps, each offset k meaning angle = baseAngle + k * (step / distance) in radians (converted to degrees), with step = 2 * rho_drawn + body.gap (V1.1). Radial offsets are the OUTER loop, angular the inner.
An angular candidate must lie inside the pool's sector [start, start + span], inclusive.
The first candidate without collision wins. If there is none, the body is overflow: placed on field.overflowRadius at its base angle, counted, not drawn.
The person constellation: rings fill in order, ring k holds floor(2 * pi * ringRadii[k] / constellation.spacing) nodes; the rest is counted.
